findings.message: sum(values) converts a huge int to float when the list also holds a float, and Python raises OverflowError. The CLI then reports an internal error instead of a positioned Pebble error, violating ADR-001 and ADR-014. Catch OverflowError around the total and report it as a too-large float.
The sum guard tests cover a non-finite float total and an oversized int total, but not a huge int mixed with a float, which is the case that escapes as a host OverflowError. Add that regression case.
findings.patch_old:
def test_sum_refuses_a_non_finite_float_result(self) -> None:
        error = self.eval_error('sum([float("1e308"), float("1e308")])')
        self.assertIn("the result is too large for a float", error.message)
        self.assertIn("beyond the largest float", error.why)
findings.patch_new:
def test_sum_refuses_a_non_finite_float_result(self) -> None:
        error = self.eval_error('sum([float("1e308"), float("1e308")])')
        self.assertIn("the result is too large for a float", error.message)
        self.assertIn("beyond the largest float", error.why)

    def test_sum_of_a_huge_int_and_a_float_is_a_pebble_error(self) -> None:
        error = self.eval_error("sum([10 ^ 3990, 1.5])")
        self.assertIn("the result is too large for a float", error.message)
        self.assertIn("no float value", error.why)

Multiplying a huge int by a float raises Python OverflowError before _check_result can run, so (10 ^ 3990) * 1.5 reaches the CLI internal-error shield instead of a positioned Pebble error. The working tree now catches OverflowError around the multiplication.

Taking the remainder of a huge int and a float raises Python OverflowError before _check_result can run, so (10 ^ 3990) % 1.5 reaches the CLI internal-error shield instead of a positioned Pebble error. The working tree now catches OverflowError around the remainder.
The hardening tests cover non-finite float results but not a huge int mixed with a float, which is the path that still raised a host OverflowError. The working tree now covers +, -, *, and %.

The comment scanner advances the index without advancing the column, so a comment at end of file leaves the EOF token at the comment's start column. A parse error at EOF after a trailing comment therefore points at the wrong column. Advance with the shared skip helper.
findings.patch_new: self._skip(1)

findings.message: The comment test checks token pairs but not the EOF position after a trailing comment, which is the case the stale column affects. Add assertions for a comment after a value and a comment-only source.
findings.patch_old:
def test_comments_run_to_the_end_of_the_line(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(pairs("# note\n42 # trailing\n# last"), [("NUMBER", 42)])
findings.patch_new:
def test_comments_run_to_the_end_of_the_line(self) -> None:
        self.assertEqual(pairs("# note\n42 # trailing\n# last"), [("NUMBER", 42)])
        self.assertEqual(tokenize("1 # x")[-1], Token("EOF", None, 1, 6))
        self.assertEqual(tokenize("# x")[-1], Token("EOF", None, 1, 4))
